_doc: No Law: the script for the voiced lines (#807). The same shape as sheriff_road.json (its _doc and docs/scripts/README.md say the fields). Built lines are copied from config/moments/no_law_murder.json unchanged. Nothing here is approved until Sean taps Script OK.
title: No Law
mission: no-law (#773 built the murder; #796 is step 4, the morning after and the sheriff's last day)
status: draft: waiting on Sean's Script OK
sources: config/moments/no_law_murder.json (the built lines, fixed); config/card_game.json (the table's talk, built)
docs/missions/no-law.md (PR #743's branch), #796 and its comments (Cody kills Earl; the red shirt is Kett and isn't in the saloon)
docs/story/OUTLINE.md Act I, VOICES.md (the foreman, Cody, the barkeep, the Baron, the widow, smaller voices), SETUPS.md, WORDS.md (PR #833)
#830: C10 b (the stranger is the Baron's foreman; nobody says so), C12 a, C14 c (roles only)
notes: Harlan doesn't speak: he's sat, unarmed, held (Sean: 'he can't do anything at all').
The sheriff's last day (Beat 5) is No Law's in the game (#796) but its lines are in the sheriff's script (scene 5, day2.*), so his voice is in one place.
The card game's talk at the table (config/card_game.json: 'Ante.', 'Call.', Earl's 'Lady's been kind tonight') is built and belongs on a town-life page later, not here.
Nobody names the red shirt (Kett) or says the stranger works for the Baron (K3, K11). The foreman's voice is open (s21): written to his built lines, calm and low.
The built _doc in no_law_murder.json still calls Cody 'the red shirt, the man who shot the sheriff': out of date since #796's comments (gameplay's file, untouched).

words_to_check.worry: WORDS.md: to check (a cattleman's word for a homesteader).

setups.what: "Ain't no law left in this valley to save you now."
Cody, the witness (the barman knows him by name; a whole room saw)
Graves: Earl's a recorded death; the sheriff's grave

setups.status: the funeral's part P·bible: he stands behind the Baron, silent

cast.name: The stranger (the Baron's foreman)
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The Baron's foreman; s21 open
cast.brief: About fifty, Western, calm and low; friendly the way a man is who can afford it. Few words, never hurried, never raised. Educated or a cowman is Sean's call (s21): the built lines lean educated.

cast.name: Cody
cast.brief: Late twenties, a Texas cowhand gone bad. Loud and short, brave with drink and a crew behind him; a hard flat voice, a sneer in it.

cast.name: Earl
cast.brief: Sixties, a card player, thin and placating; quick to smile, quicker to apologise.

cast.name: The barkeep
cast.brief: Forties, aggrieved and quick, always counting what a thing costs him; a nasal Midwestern voice that rises when he's upset.

cast.name: The drifter
cast.brief: Thirties, a hand between jobs; dry, low, wants no part of anything.

cast.name: The miner at the table
cast.brief: Fifties, a hard-rock man, slow and heavy, a little Cornish (WORDS.md: 'my son' once is enough).

cast.name: A townsman
cast.bible: P·bible (No Law's Beat 1, the town without a sheriff)
cast.brief: Forties, a storekeeper type; worried, talks low, glances over his shoulder.

cast.name: A townswoman
cast.brief: Thirties to forties, plain-spoken, good grammar; brisk, says what she thinks.

cast.name: A bold man in the street
cast.bible: No Law's Beat 1: 'others behave more boldly'
cast.brief: Thirties, a teamster or a hand in town; too loud, a little drunk, enjoying the sheriff's absence.

cast.name: The undertaker
cast.brief: Sixties, unhurried, precise, a dry gallows humour he doesn't know he has.

cast.name: The preacher
cast.brief: Fifties, a Methodist circuit man; carrying voice, plain, unadorned; reads the old words without performing them.

cast.name: The Baron
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The Baron; WORDS.md, The Baron
cast.brief: Sixty, educated, courteous and unhurried; long sentences, never a threat. Eastern or British money: his accent is Sean's call.

cast.name: The sheriff's wife
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The widow (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: About forty, a Midwestern farm wife with good schooling. Level and low, short; grief held under work.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner; brisk, quiet, dry.

scenes.title: Salt Creek without its sheriff
scenes.setting: The sheriff is at the doctor's. Townsfolk at their evening posts talk about it; some are worried, some bolder for it. Who sends Harlan to the saloon is open (s26): Sean's two ways are written below, both proposed.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: You pass him on Main Street, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Low, to his neighbour more than to you.

words.text: Sheriff's shot, they say. Laid up at the doc's.
Who's to keep the peace now? Not me.
I'm putting the bar on my door tonight.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: You pass her on Main Street, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Shaking out a cloth; plain sympathy, no gossip in it.

words.text: That poor woman. Fourteen years on that claim, and now this.
Somebody ought to ride out and sit with the boys.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: You pass him by the saloon, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Too loud, pleased with himself; the street goes quiet around him.

words.text: No sheriff tonight, boys. Drink where you please.
Who's going to fine me? The doc?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Sizing you up; half thanks, half suspicion.

words.text: You're the one brought him in. From up the creek.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Just passing on the news.

words.text: Freighter found him in the road, they say. Left there like a dead dog.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: Leaving the doctor's that evening (after evening.doctor.go in the sheriff's script)
lines.note: s26, one of Sean's two ways: someone tells him to go
lines.delivery: An afterthought at the door.

words.text: Get yourself a drink at the saloon, Harlan. You've earned one, and I can't prescribe you anything better.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: He falls in beside you on Main Street, evening of day 1
lines.note: s26, Sean's other way: the stranger brings him
lines.delivery: Easy, as if you'd known each other years; already walking you there.

words.text: Evening. You look like a man who could stand a drink. I'm buying.

scenes.title: The table
scenes.when: Night 1, the saloon's yard, the card table
scenes.setting: Harlan is sat at the card table, unarmed. A minute before Cody comes, the stranger takes the free chair and puts his hand on Harlan's arm. (The table's own talk is built and goes on a town-life page.)

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: He sits in the free chair beside you (a minute before Cody)
lines.delivery: Pleasant, unhurried, a man settling in for the evening.

words.text: Evening. Mind if I sit in a while?

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: Cody comes into the yard; the stranger's hand on your arm
lines.delivery: Low, close, not looking at you; the friendliness gone flat.

words.text: Don't move, friend. Whatever happens next, you sit still.

scenes.title: The murder
scenes.setting: Cody walks up, accuses Earl, kicks his chair out from under him and shoots him in the head where he lies. Very quick; not a fair fight. The room goes quiet until the barman.

lines.speaker: cody
lines.trigger: Cody comes into the yard: shouting at Earl from the moment he walks in, before he reaches the table
lines.delivery: Shouted across the yard as he comes, already worked up; the whole room turns. The no-law line comes after, quiet, with Earl on the floor.

words.text: Earl, you cheating son of a bitch!
words.note: Sean's redo, 2026-11-12 (was the built 'Earl. You been dealing off the bottom of that deck.')

lines.speaker: earl
lines.trigger: Right after the accusation
lines.delivery: A nervous smile in it; cut off by the kick.

words.text: Now, Cody, I never...

lines.speaker: cody
lines.trigger: Over Earl on the ground, after the shot
lines.delivery: Not shouted: almost conversational, a man who knows nobody will stop him.

words.text: Ain't no law left in this valley to save you now, Earl.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: The hush after Cody turns away
lines.delivery: Outraged about the wrong thing; the first sound in the room. Sean's punchline: play it straight.

words.text: Jesus, Cody, my chair!

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: At Earl's body, ~20 s later
lines.delivery: Starts to give an order and finds there's nobody to give it to.

words.text: Somebody ought to fetch the... hell. Ain't nobody left to fetch.

scenes.title: After
scenes.when: Night 1, the saloon's yard and the street
scenes.setting: Cody walks out; the drifter and the miner leave; the stranger has his word and goes. Earl's body stays. Harlan can try to help Earl (shot through the head), and can follow Cody out and see which way he rides. Built: the stranger's lines. New: the rest.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: Cody's out of the yard; the stranger stands to go
lines.delivery: Friendly again, which is worse; a hand on your shoulder as he passes.

words.text: You didn't see a thing tonight. Nobody did. Remember that.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: You point a gun at him
lines.delivery: Unbothered; he's had guns pointed at him before.

words.text: Easy, friend. I ain't the one you want.
Put it up. You'll only get yourself killed.
Walk away. That's my advice.

lines.speaker: drifter
lines.trigger: He gets up to leave (~5 s after Cody's out)
lines.delivery: Picking up his hat, to nobody.

words.text: I never saw nothing. I was never here.

lines.speaker: miner
lines.trigger: He gets up to leave (~9 s after Cody's out)
lines.delivery: Looking down at Earl a long moment.

words.text: Was he cheating? ... Hell. What odds does it make now.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: You kneel by Earl
lines.delivery: Telling you what you can already see.

words.text: Leave him, Harlan. He's past anybody's help.
Through the head. There's nothing to be done.

lines.speaker: cody
lines.trigger: You follow him out to the street; he's mounting
lines.delivery: Doesn't even look round; then he rides for the foothills.

words.text: Go on back to your cards, nester.

scenes.title: The morning after
scenes.when: Day 2, morning, Main Street (#796, not built)
scenes.setting: The town wakes to the news. Earl goes to the undertaker's as a recorded death. Townsfolk tell the night differently, by what you saw of it (nolaw.seen_from: table / yard / heard / away). Nobody arrests Cody. Then someone sends for Harlan: the sheriff is dying.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: You pass him on day 2
lines.delivery: Each telling a little surer of itself than the last.

words.text: Cody shot Earl dead over the cards. Said there's no law left to save him. Bold as brass.
Earl drew first, I heard. Or reached, anyhow.
Three shots, they say. Or two. Nobody counted.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: You pass her on day 2
lines.delivery: Disapproving of the whole saloon and everyone in it.

words.text: A dozen men sat there and watched it. Not one of them stood up.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you on day 2
lines.delivery: Not loud; he wants an answer and doesn't expect one.

words.text: You were sat right there at the table, they say. And you never moved.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: You pass him on day 2
lines.delivery: Last night's bravado gone sour.

words.text: And who's to take Cody in? The sheriff's dying.
He'll be back, you watch. Nobody to stop him.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the undertaker's, Earl laid out
lines.delivery: Writing in his book as he talks; reads the entry back to himself.

words.text: Earl. Shot through the head, before witnesses, by the man Cody. Pine box. Nobody's paying for a stone.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He finds you on day 2 (the doctor sent him)
lines.delivery: Out of breath from looking for you.

words.text: Harlan! Doc's asking for you. Says the sheriff's sinking.

lines.note: Then the sheriff's last day: the sheriff's script, scene 5 (day2.*)

scenes.title: The funeral
scenes.when: Day 2 or 3, the cemetery on the hill (Beat 6, not built)
scenes.setting: Quiet, not a set piece. The town gathers; hats come off. The Baron offers the widow a price for her claim at the graveside, the foreman behind him saying nothing (S39). Harlan can attend, watch from a distance or miss it.

lines.speaker: preacher
lines.trigger: The service at the grave
lines.delivery: The old burial words, read plainly into the wind; no performance.

words.text: Man that is born of a woman hath but a short time to live, and is full of misery. He cometh up, and is cut down, like a flower.
words.note: the Book of Common Prayer's burial service (1662), public domain

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Among the mourners, after
lines.delivery: Hat in his hands; a small true thing about the dead man.

words.text: Fined me twice. Fair, both times.
He'd come in Saturdays. One drink. Never two.

lines.speaker: baron
lines.trigger: At the graveside, after the service, to the widow; you're near enough to hear
lines.delivery: Hat in hand, voice lowered, perfectly kind. Nothing in it you could object to.

words.text: A hard day, ma'am. When that place grows too much for you, come to me first. You'll not find a fairer figure.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: Her answer to the Baron
lines.delivery: Not raised. She doesn't look at him.

words.text: Not today. Not any day.

lines.speaker: baron
lines.trigger: He passes you on his way out
lines.delivery: Already knows your name; lets you see that he does.

words.text: Mr. Harlan. A sad day for the county.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: As the mourners go
lines.delivery: Brief; she has a hundred hands to shake.

words.text: You came, Mr. Harlan. He'd have noticed that.
